transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-23 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mayer (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Sterling Head of Platform), Mark O'Neal (ML Eng), Sofia Chen (SRE), Tom Brooks (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and KV/prefix caching recommendations. Reviewed cost model assumptions, trade-offs for TTL and prefetch, sample sim results, and pilot next steps.

[00:00] Alex Mayer: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we have about 45 minutes, we'll run through a compact ops sprint for batching and the kv-based prefix caching approach and then leave time for q a. is that cool?
[00:18] Nina Patel: yep that's perfect, we've got some key constraints — 99th p90 latency goals, and we care about per-invoice cost more than absolute throughput, so cost per 1k tokens matters.
[00:30] Priya Desai: okay great, i'll start with a quick mental model then show the console sim. forgive any background noise; i'm in transit but should be fine.
[00:45] Priya Desai: so core idea — two levers we usually tune: batching (how many concurrent requests we pack per microbatch) and prefix/KV caching (how much of user context we persist between requests so we avoid re-decoding). these combine non-linearly for cost. small batch sizes favor latency but increase tokens; big batches amortize compute.
[01:12] Mark O'Neal: when you say "kv caching" are you referring to session KV or prefix-only? our flows have a lot of short-lived sessions but with repeated prompts for tracking shipments.
[01:25] Priya Desai: good question — for Sterling i'd recommend a hybrid: prefix cache for the static context (policy, templates) with short TTLs for session KV for active flows. that captures most hit-rate without indefinite retention.
[01:40] Carlos Ruiz: i'll throw up the sim we prepared — slides linked in chat; shows three scenarios: baseline (no cache, batch size 1), moderate (batch 4 + prefix cache 30s TTL), aggressive (batch 8 + prefix 5m TTL).
[01:58] Sofia Chen: five minutes ttl sounds risky for data residency and retention, we have to check legal. also we can't exceed 7 days retention.
[02:10] Alex Mayer: totally — pause on TTL governance. the console supports TTL policies per-namespace and automatic anonymization hooks; we can set retention to 30s to 24h depending on workload. we'll include that in the compliance packet.
[02:28] Priya Desai: back to econ — with your median prompt length (~120 tokens) and expected response (~220 tokens) our sim shows: baseline cost X, moderate saves ~28% cost, aggressive saves ~44% but latency 95th jumps from 180ms to 320ms. numbers in the workbook.
[02:52] Nina Patel: that's useful. can you unpack how batching affects KV cache pressure and mem requirements? we have limited reserved GPU memory on our Dedicated clusters.
[03:06] Carlos Ruiz: batching increases concurrent KV footprints because multiple sequences may reference the KV cache. our runtime does shared KV eviction prioritization — but net memory scales roughly with active sessions * average KV size. if average prefix is 3kb and hit rate 60% you can expect 1.8kb effective per session. rough math in the sim.
[03:34] Mark O'Neal: any guidance on batch formation latency controls? we can't add tail latency beyond 50ms.
[03:41] Priya Desai: we recommend adaptive batching: set a max microbatch wait of 15ms and max microbatch size of 4 for latency-sensitive routes. for background or summary gen, you can up to 8-12. console exposes these knobs and the Optimize module suggests defaults based on your p95 target.
[04:03] Tom Brooks: how does prefix caching interact with streaming? we stream tokens to the user as they arrive.
[04:12] Priya Desai: good point. prefix cache is used in KV for decode so streaming is compatible; streaming simply flushes tokens as they are produced. the only caveat is if you prefetch KV from disk there's a tiny addition on cold starts (10-20ms).
[04:28] Nina Patel: are there quantization trade-offs we should know about? we push smaller models to save cost sometimes.
[04:36] Carlos Ruiz: yes — lower-precision quant (4-bit/8-bit) reduces memory and improves throughput which synergizes with batching. but it can raise subtle quality regressions; Optimize will flag model-regression on pre-defined evals and recommend switching fallback routes.
[04:55] [05:00] Alex Mayer: let's run a concrete example: take 10k daily active users, average 3 requests/day, 340 tokens per session. with moderate setup (batch 4, prefix 30s) you end up ~32% monthly cost reduction versus baseline hosted without cache. numbers depend on hit-rate and session churn — we'll share spreadsheet.
[05:25] Mark O'Neal: can you rerun the sim using our real heatmap? we can export TTLs and session durations.
[05:33] Priya Desai: absolutely — that's part of the pilot. ask you for 2 weeks of traffic, we'll run sandbox sim and produce an adjusted savings estimate.
[05:45] Nina Patel: security/regulatory — we need SOC2 + SSO integration and audit logs for any Private deployment. does Redwood's Private offer HSM/KMS?
[05:55] Alex Mayer: yes, Private supports KMS integration and optional HSM. audit logs and per-request provenance are available. we'll attach the security whitepaper and a compliance matrix.
[06:10] Sofia Chen: on the performance side, we need to know about fallback behavior when a Dedicated pool is saturated. do you auto-route to hosted variants?
[06:20] Carlos Ruiz: yes you can configure smart routing policies — prefer Dedicated, then fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant or a quantized replica. fallbacks are policy-driven; you can prefer latency or cost depending on business rules.
[06:35] Priya Desai: i want to call out a pattern that saved another logistics customer: keep a short prefix cache for templates and a separate session-cold cache for rare but heavy state. this gave them 25% savings while avoiding privacy risks.
[06:52] Mark O'Neal: how do you recommend we split the cache keys? by customer-id then session-id? we have multi-tenant routing.
[07:00] Priya Desai: namespace by tenant, key by truncated prompt hash + template id; that way eviction is tenant-aware and prevents one tenant from skewing memory. also include per-tenant TTL defaults in the namespace.
[07:18] Tom Brooks: any gotchas for sharded KV? we use a sharded Redis cluster in front of things.
[07:25] Carlos Ruiz: sharded stores are fine — Redwood runtime expects eventually consistent cache reads; we recommend co-locating KV in the same zone as the serving instances to avoid cross-az latencies. console will surface miss rates per shard.
[07:45] [08:02] Nina Patel: ok can we talk about experiment design for pilot? what should success metrics be?
[08:10] Priya Desai: success metrics: % cost reduction vs baseline, p95 latency delta, cache hit-rate, and user-facing quality regressions (difflog/ROUGE or your internal metric). set thresholds: >20% cost reduction with p95 delta < 15% is a good target.
[08:30] Mark O'Neal: and we'd want rollbacks automated if quality dips past threshold. does Redwood support automatic fallback to previous model/version?
[08:39] Alex Mayer: yes canary rollouts with automatic quality monitoring; you can set an eval suite and automatic rollback triggers.
[08:49] Sofia Chen: about instrumentation: what traces do you need from our side? we run honeycomb and datadog.
[08:58] Carlos Ruiz: we'll need per-request latencies, token counts, and session ids. we can ingest traces into Datadog or export spans; there's also a lightweight SDK.
[09:12] [09:30] Priya Desai: quick demo time — i'm going to share my screen. apologies if the demo lags a bit.
[09:35] Priya Desai: here's the Optimize console: the savings simulator, input fields (median tokens, responses, batch size, TTLs, expected concurrency). i'll change batch size from 1 to 4 and show delta.
[09:54] [10:10] Priya Desai: see this column — cost per 1k tokens baseline vs with prefix cache. you can toggle hit rates; with a 50% hit rate you get about 22% savings at batch 4. if you push hit-rate to 70% the savings jump to ~35%.
[10:30] Nina Patel: can you export these numbers to csv? we'll forward to finance.
[10:35] Priya Desai: yep export button, also a "share workbook" link that we can populate with your traffic and rerun.
[10:44] Tom Brooks: curious about billing granularity — per token, per inference, or a blended reserved+usage?
[10:51] Alex Mayer: for hosted it's usage-based per-token; Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts plus overage usage; Optimize can show blended unit economics for either. we'll include pricing scenarios in the sheet.
[11:05] Mark O'Neal: do you charge for KV storage separately?
[11:09] Carlos Ruiz: KV storage is included in Dedicated reservations up to a threshold; for Hosted there's a small storage surcharge for high retention volumes. we'll highlight it in the workbook.
[11:22] [12:00] Nina Patel: ok i realize we need to confirm a few internal items: 1) retention policy 2) which models we want to test (we prefer 4-bit quantized medium models for most flows) 3) pilot timeline — can target early May.
[12:16] Alex Mayer: that aligns — we'll send a proposed pilot plan with dates.
[12:22] Priya Desai: one more operational note: set microbatch wait <= 20ms for checkout flows, <=50ms for conversational. the console has pre-defined profiles for ecom-checkout and support-chat.
[12:40] Mark O'Neal: we have an internal cost goal to reduce inference spend by 30% in Q3. if you can demonstrate 25-40% on our pilot that would be compelling for Dedicated consideration.
[12:53] Alex Mayer: understood — we'll focus the pilot on the high-volume routes with the best hit-rate potential.
[13:05] [13:30] Sofia Chen: any dependencies on our infra? we'd rather avoid opening up VPC peering immediately; can sandbox run over internet endpoints?
[13:40] Carlos Ruiz: sandbox can run over internet endpoints for initial tests. for Private we do VPC peering or on-prem appliance later.
[13:52] Nina Patel: ok last question — are there any known regressions when combining high batching with long TTLs? we worry about stale context being used.
[14:02] Priya Desai: stale context risk is real; we recommend versioned prefix keys and freshness checks — e.g., include last-modified timestamp in the key and TTL; Optimize flags low-quality drift and can auto-expire prefixes if quality drops.
[14:20] Alex Mayer: time check — we have ~6 minutes left. quick recap and next steps?
[14:28] Alex Mayer: recap: Redwood recommends hybrid prefix+session KV, adaptive batching (max microbatch wait 15ms, size 4 for sensitive), pilot to run sandbox sim with your heatmap, security docs and pricing workbook to be shared.
[14:42] Nina Patel: that's good. any blockers on your side?
[14:45] Alex Mayer: none. we'll send calendar invite for pilot kickoff and the workbook.
[14:51] Tom Brooks: thanks all, this was helpful.
[14:55] [15:00] Meeting ends.
